### Granfondo Via del Sale
Tier 2 | Score: 60/100 | 97 mi | 7,260 ft | Cervia, Emilia-Romagna, Italy | March | gran_fondo
Profile: https://roadielabs.com/race/granfondo-via-del-sale/
Markdown: https://roadielabs.com/race/granfondo-via-del-sale.md

The Salt Road. From Cervia's ancient salt pans to the Romagna hills. Pantani showed up at the first one. A road gran fondo that traces the ancient salt trading route from the Adriatic coast into the Romagna hills. The route starts flat from Cervia at sea level, passes the historic salt pans, and heads inland through rolling countryside to a series of punchy climbs. The hills are not long — the longest is 10 km — but gradients reach 18%. The rhythm is distinctive: flat coastal start, progressive climbing through the Romagna foothills, emotional climax at Cima Pantani, a final timed climb, and 32 km of flat back to the Adriatic finish. The salt road runs both ways. Signature challenge: Cima Pantani on Montevecchio — not the longest or the steepest climb, but the one that matters. 373m of gain at up to 14% with Pantani's name painted on the road. The Grand Prix Via del Sale is awarded here. But the real challenge is cumulative: five distinct climbs across 156 km, with the timed segment at Paderno-Collinello coming after 85+ miles of riding. The salt road demands endurance, not just climbing power. The Granfondo Via del Sale traces the ancient route of Cervia's salt miners — from the Adriatic coast's salt pans into the Romagna hills. Twenty-nine editions, a famously low entry fee, and the legend of Marco Pantani showing up unannounced at the first race in 1997. The climbs are not Alpine — Monte Cavallo at 438m, Ciola at 557m — but gradients reach 18% on Santa Maria Riopetra, and Cima Pantani on Montevecchio has 'VAI MARCO... FORZA PIRATA' painted on the road where the champion once rode. This is a solid Italian gran fondo at an exceptional price point, steeped in salt and cycling history. Yes if you want an affordable, well-established Italian gran fondo with genuine historical narrative and a Pantani pilgrimage. Yes if punchy Romagna hills with 18% gradients at EUR35 sounds like your kind of value. Skip if you want Alpine spectacle — these are foothills, not mountains. Skip if you need a large international field — this is an Italian event for Italian cyclists.

### L'Etape Australia by Tour de France
Tier 2 | Score: 60/100 | 98 mi | 9,088 ft | Wollongong to Kiama, New South Wales, Australia | December | gran_fondo
Profile: https://roadielabs.com/race/letape-australia/
Markdown: https://roadielabs.com/race/letape-australia.md

The Tour de France comes to Australia -- when it actually happens. Mountainous coastal road course replicating a Tour de France stage -- 143 km with 2,701 m of climbing on fully closed sealed roads through the NSW South Coast, Shoalhaven, and Illawarra escarpment. Signature challenge: Two ascents of Macquarie Pass (Race) separated by 40+ km of rolling terrain -- the second climb at 70+ km on tired legs is where the event is won and lost. L'Etape Australia brings Tour de France branding and ASO production values to the NSW South Coast -- 143 km of fully closed roads, 2,701 m of climbing, classification jerseys, Shimano support, and 3,000+ riders chasing the yellow jersey dream. Chris Froome rode the inaugural edition in the Snowy Mountains in 2016. The experience is genuinely special: cowbells, closed roads, professional timing, and that unmistakable TdF atmosphere. But this event has been plagued by cancellations -- severe weather, council opposition, road landslips -- to the point where showing up and actually racing feels like an achievement in itself. The move from the spectacular Snowy Mountains to the Wollongong-Kiama coastal route was forced by local politics, not course design ambition. At ~$300 AUD it is expensive for a sportive, though the included jersey and full support soften that. If you can actually get to a start line that exists, the riding is excellent. If you are based in Australia and want the closest thing to riding a Tour de France stage without leaving the Southern Hemisphere, this is your event. The 143 km course with 2,701 m of climbing on fully closed roads is a genuine challenge, the TdF atmosphere is infectious, and the included jersey is a legitimate keepsake. But you need to accept the cancellation risk: this event has been cancelled three times in four years. Do not book non-refundable international flights. Do not build your entire season around it. Train for it, enter it, hope for the best, and have a backup Australian sportive on your calendar. If you are traveling from overseas specifically for this event, consider the original L'Etape du Tour in France instead -- same brand, better reliability, more iconic climbs.

### L'Etape Czech Republic by Tour de France
Tier 2 | Score: 60/100 | 82 mi | 5,577 ft | Prague and Central Bohemia Region, Czech Republic | June | gran_fondo
Profile: https://roadielabs.com/race/letape-czech-republic/
Markdown: https://roadielabs.com/race/letape-czech-republic.md

ASO's Tour de France franchise in Prague: 3,000 riders on closed Bohemian roads, strong organization, and Europe's best post-ride beer. Rolling Bohemian countryside on fully closed roads. The hilly stage winds through the Central Bohemia region, passing through the Krivoklat forests, Berounsko river valley, and the Czech Karst -- a landscape of limestone formations, deep forests, ancient alleys, and historic villages. The terrain is characterized by punchy hills rather than sustained mountain climbs: categorized ascents of 2-5 km with gradients that reward explosive power as much as steady-state climbing. The 2024 edition introduced four new summits to freshen the route. Descents wind through forested sections on well-maintained roads. The course delivers a classic European hilly sportive profile -- genuinely challenging but not destructive. Signature challenge: The accumulated vertical across punchy Bohemian hills. No single climb is a monster, but 1,700 m of elevation gain delivered in short, sharp efforts across rolling terrain demands repeated high-intensity efforts. The long route's 25 km/h minimum average time limit adds pressure -- you cannot soft-pedal the hills and expect to make cutoff. L'Etape Czech Republic delivers a polished Tour de France experience on fully closed roads through the scenic Bohemian countryside, starting and finishing in one of Europe's most appealing capitals. The organization -- under ASO patronage and run by Petr Cech Sport -- is genuinely impressive for a 6-year-old event: closed roads, classification jerseys, Shimano support, celebrity riders, and thousands of enthusiastic Czech fans lining the route. Bradley Wiggins rode the 2025 edition and praised the atmosphere. The course through Krivoklat forests and the Czech Karst is beautiful, if not brutal -- 1,700 m of climbing over 132 km is honest work but not Alpine suffering. The year-round Bootcamp community program is a smart differentiator that builds loyalty beyond race day. Prague as a host city is the real bonus: affordable, beautiful, excellent food and beer, direct flights from everywhere. Yes if you want a professionally organized, closed-road sportive with Tour de France branding in one of Europe's most appealing and affordable cities. Yes if you want the L'Etape experience without Alpine-scale suffering. Skip if you need Alpine passes and 5,000 m of climbing to feel challenged. Skip if you want a globally prestigious event with international field depth -- this is still regional.

A festive, accessible urban cycling celebration in Eastern Europe's premier amateur Tour de France event. Urban loop through Bucharest's historic heart on fully closed roads; celebratory, accessible, and landmark-rich rather than technically demanding Signature challenge: Maintaining momentum through dense urban sections and navigating 2,500+ cyclists on closed roads; psychological challenge of distance (85 km) rather than terrain difficulty L'Étape Romania is an excellent entry point into the official Tour de France amateur series, combining accessibility, urban charm, and pro-level logistics. L'Étape Romania delivers a well-organized, inclusive amateur cycling experience with strong community spirit and official Tour de France credibility. The fully closed roads through iconic Bucharest landmarks, three distance options, and Race Village create a festival atmosphere that appeals to all levels. However, the flat urban course lacks elevation challenge and technical difficulty, limiting appeal for experienced cyclists seeking a demanding ride. The qualification pathway to L'Étape du Tour in France and modest registration costs enhance value. Recommended for first-time amateurs, families, and cyclists prioritizing experience and community over physical challenge.

### Gran Fondo Pekan / Pekan Classic

A real Gran Fondo World Series stop in Pahang with a flat river route and one hilly loop — but 2026 status is unconfirmed. Per the organizer's own course report: 'both sides of the flat borders of the Pahang river during the first 40km and the last 68km,' with a hillier backcountry middle section (roughly 55km) supplying most of the route's climbing. Overall officially described as 'flat and fast' — 162.7 km with 1,072 m of climbing and a maximum single peak of just 84m (not the 762 m previously listed here). A shorter Medio Fondo (93.5 km / 470 m, mostly along the river borders) serves as the age-category route for older riders (men 60+, women 50+) rather than an open fitness-level choice. Signature challenge: Holding pace on a genuinely flat, fast 162.7 km course where the modest 1,072 m of climbing is spread as gentle backcountry undulation (max peak 84m) rather than any single defined climb — the challenge is speed and heat management, not technical terrain. Pekan Classics is a UCI Gran Fondo World Series event confirmed on both uci.org and the official World Series calendar — its debut and, so far, only confirmed edition ran 20 June 2025 (803 riders from 18 countries, per the organizer's own report), not the 2023 debut this listing previously implied. The Gran Fondo distance is 162.7 km with 1,072 m of climbing on an organizer-described 'flat and fast' course (max single peak 84m); this listing previously understated the climbing at 762 m. No 2026 edition has been confirmed: a third-party calendar floated 19 June 2026 but marked it explicitly unconfirmed, that date has passed with no results or report, the event is absent from the current UCI/World Series 2026 calendar, and the organizer's own domain was unreachable during this research. None of that amounts to a formal cancellation, but a rider should treat it as a real, unresolved hiatus rather than a confirmed annual fixture. If a 2026 or later edition is confirmed by the organizer, yes for riders wanting an approachable, mostly-flat World Series stop. Don't commit travel plans on the strength of the current unconfirmed 19 June 2026 date alone.

### Race Around Ireland
Tier 2 | Score: 60/100 | 1340.7 mi | 72,178 ft | Trim, County Meath, Ireland | — | gran_fondo
Profile: https://roadielabs.com/race/race-around-ireland/
Markdown: https://roadielabs.com/race/race-around-ireland.md

A real Irish circumnavigation ultra with an 11-edition history — that hasn't run since 2019. A real, distinct ultra-endurance ROAD CYCLING race — not to be confused with the Wicklow Sailing Club's separate 'Round Ireland Race' offshore yacht race, a different sport run by a different organization. Race Around Ireland is a single-stage, continuous-clock circumnavigation of the island: an anticlockwise loop starting and finishing in Trim, County Meath, passing Newgrange/Brú na Bóinne, the Causeway Coast, Malin Head, Connemara, the Cliffs of Moher, the Ring of Kerry, Mizen Head, the Wexford coast, and the Wicklow Mountains before returning to Trim. It is supported, not self-supported — every rider or team must run a minimum three-person crew with a following vehicle, whose crews phone in check-ins at 21 unmanned time stations along an unmarked route navigated by route book. Solo riders (men and women), tandems, and 2/4/8-person relay teams all race the same course on the same continuous clock, which runs through all sleep, food, and mechanical stops. The race last ran in 2019 (its 11th edition) and has not run since — it was cancelled in 2020, 2021, and 2022, and the organizer's own January 2022 cancellation notice, while stating the race 'will come back in the future,' gives no return date and none has surfaced through 2026. Signature challenge: Completing a full, continuous, ~2,150 km lap of Ireland's coastline inside a hard 132-hour (solo men) or 144-hour (solo women) clock — not a single climb or sector, but the accumulated sleep deprivation and roughly 22,000 m of climbing across four-plus days without a stage break. Race Around Ireland is a genuine ultra-endurance road race — a continuous, supported circumnavigation of Ireland from Trim, roughly 2,150-2,160 km and 22,000 m of climbing, run 11 times between 2009 and 2019. It is a completely different event from the Wicklow Sailing Club's similarly-named offshore yacht race, and a prior audit pass on this profile wrongly concluded otherwise — that was a research error, not a fact about the race. The real problem with this listing today isn't identity, it's currency: the race has not run since 2019. It was cancelled in 2020, 2021, and again in January 2022, when the organizer said the event 'will come back in the future' without giving a date. No 2023, 2024, 2025, or 2026 announcement, results, or working registration turned up in this research — though official social channels are only partially indexable, so a comeback announced solely there could be missed. Not currently possible — no edition has been held or announced since 2019, and the organizer's last public word (Jan 2022) gave no return date. Watch racearoundireland.com for an actual comeback announcement before planning around this.

### Ring of Kerry Charity Cycle
Tier 2 | Score: 60/100 | 112 mi | 5,774 ft | Killarney, County Kerry, Ireland | July | gran_fondo
Profile: https://roadielabs.com/race/ring-of-kerry-charity-cycle/
Markdown: https://roadielabs.com/race/ring-of-kerry-charity-cycle.md

170 km around the Iveragh Peninsula. Ireland's biggest one-day cycling event. EUR 22 million raised. The Atlantic coast is the scenery. Charity is the point. A counterclockwise loop around the Iveragh Peninsula on Ireland's Atlantic seaboard. The route leaves Killarney heading west through Killorglin, follows the coast south through Cahersiveen, Waterville, and Caherdaniel, climbs Coomakista for Skellig views, continues east through Sneem to Kenmare, then returns to Killarney via Moll's Gap — the highest and toughest climb of the day. The terrain is rolling throughout with two significant climbs. The character alternates between exposed Atlantic coast road and sheltered inland valleys. It is not an extreme route by European granfondo standards, but 170 km with 1,760m of climbing and the possibility of Atlantic headwinds makes it a demanding day for recreational riders. Signature challenge: Moll's Gap at 140 km — the highest point on the route with poor road surface and steady gradient. It is the moment when under-prepared riders discover that 170 km of Atlantic coast riding has consequences. The climb itself is moderate, but the context is not. The Ring of Kerry Charity Cycle is not a race. It has no timing chips, no results board, no podium. What it has is 44 years of history, EUR 22 million raised for 200+ charities, 1,200 volunteers who make the roads of Kerry safe for thousands of cyclists, and 170 km of Atlantic coast scenery that ranks among the most beautiful cycling routes in Europe. The Iveragh Peninsula delivers the Skellig Islands, Coomakista's ocean views, Moll's Gap, and the approach through Killarney National Park. The climbing is honest but not savage. The weather is a gamble with the Atlantic. The community spirit is not manufactured — it is the DNA of the event. Founded in 1982, this is Ireland's largest one-day cycling event and one of Europe's most significant charity rides. You do not ride the Ring of Kerry to prove anything. You ride it to contribute to something larger than yourself, and the Atlantic scenery is the reward for showing up. Yes if you want one of Europe's great scenic charity rides — the Iveragh Peninsula coastline is spectacular. Yes if community and charitable purpose matter as much as personal achievement. Skip if you need competition, timing, or race results. Skip if Atlantic weather uncertainty is a dealbreaker for a trip to western Ireland.

### Tour de Yabakei

A young, honest, untimed fan ride through a heritage-designated Japanese gorge — currently unconfirmed for 2026. A noncompetitive hill-climb fan ride through Yabakei, Hon-Yabakei and Sanko in Nakatsu, Oita — a nationally designated Place of Scenic Beauty (1923) and part of Japan Heritage story #054, "Yabakei Excursion" (recognized 2017). This is a Japanese national designation, not a UNESCO World Heritage listing. The riding mixes mountain public roads with sections of the Maple Yaba Cycling Road, built on the abandoned Yabakei Railway alignment, threading old railway tunnels and bridges through the river valley. Hon-Yabakei's landscape includes the Yamakuni River, the Ao-no-Domon tunnel, Kyoshuho cliffs, and the Rakanji rock formations and historic stone bridges, though the organizer's public materials don't specify which landmarks every route passes. Entry via Ura-Yabakei is not verified for the current course and shouldn't be assumed. Signature challenge: Repeated short, steep paved passes — up to nine on the 150km S course, seven on the 120km A course — with isolated ramps the organizer describes as exceeding 20%. Individual climbs generally gain 200-300m; no official gradient-by-gradient data or climb names have been published. Tour de Yabakei is a noncompetitive, untimed hill-climb fan ride through a Japan Heritage-designated gorge, now three editions deep (Oct 2023, May 2024, May 2025). The 2025 edition drew approximately 480 riders across four self-selected courses (150/120/70/40km) against an 800-rider combined capacity, including an official delegation from Taichung, Taiwan. It's a fan ride, not a race — no timing, no results, no ranked field. As of this verification (July 2026), no 2026 date has been announced on either the official event site or the local tourism association's calendar; status is unknown rather than confirmed-active until a new date appears. Only once a 2026 date is officially confirmed — check tourdeyabakei.studio.site and nakatsuyaba.com directly before booking travel. If it's running, it's worthwhile for scenic, self-paced climbing without race pressure.

### Utrecht Ultra
Tier 2 | Score: 60/100 | 621.4 mi | 19,685 ft | Utrecht, Netherlands (out-and-back through Belgium) | May | gran_fondo
Profile: https://roadielabs.com/race/utrecht-ultra/
Markdown: https://roadielabs.com/race/utrecht-ultra.md

Self-supported 1,000km road ultra linking Utrecht to fixed Flemish Ardennes and Belgian Ardennes checkpoint parcours within a 100-hour clock. Utrecht Ultra is a self-supported, self-navigated road ultra: a mass start from Utrecht at 18:00 on a Saturday, a 100-hour clock, and a route that is only partly fixed. The organizer publishes five fixed parcours — the Utrecht start/finish loop plus three checkpoint parcours in Belgium (an Oudenaarde-area section in the Flemish Ardennes, a section toward Dinant, and a section between La Roche-en-Ardenne and Houffalize) — that together make up roughly 60% of the advertised ~1,000km/6,000m route. Riders plan and ride their own connecting roads between those fixed sections, so no two finishers cover an identical course; the ~1,000km figure is an advertised total, not a fixed measured distance. The surface is almost entirely paved (organizer estimate ~98%). There are no staffed feed zones outside the fixed parcours — riders rely on commercial services (shops, hotels, bakeries) for the free-routed stretches. Signature challenge: Self-navigating the roughly 40% of the route that isn't fixed — plotting your own roads between the Oudenaarde, Dinant, and La Roche-Houffalize checkpoint parcours inside a hard 100-hour clock, with no organizer support once you're off the published sections. Utrecht Ultra is an organized self-supported road ultra founded in 2023 by Ruben Plat, with its own website, published start list, and a Follow My Challenge tracker used as the event's official timing/results supplier. It is not a duplicate or alias of Race Around the Netherlands (RATN): different organizer, different start city, different dates (Utrecht Ultra runs May 23-27; RATN's 2026 edition ran May 2-10), a much shorter advertised distance (~1,000km vs. RATN's ~1,950km full loop), and a shorter cutoff (100 hours vs. RATN's 202 hours). It is not a gran fondo in the conventional sense: there's a wave start and a hard 100-hour clock, and the tracker publishes finish order and times, but there's no age-category classification or prize structure, and roughly 40% of the route is left to each rider to plan and navigate themselves rather than following a marked, marshalled course. Consider it if you want a shorter, more achievable entry into self-supported ultra-distance road racing and don't need a ranked competitive field or full course support. Skip it if you're looking for a scored gran fondo experience — this is closer to a bikepacking race with a mass start.

Veloturk Gran Fondo Çeşme is a genuine, roughly decade-old road gran fondo on Turkey's Çeşme Peninsula, produced by Argeus Travel & Events with VeloTurk (a Turkish cycling group tied to a bicycle-donation social project) and listed on the Turkish Cycling Federation's official gran fondo calendar. Supported out-and-back ride from Muscat to Wadi Dayqah Dam through the Hajar foothills — non-competitive, but a real and recurring event. A supported, largely non-competitive road-cycling endurance challenge organized by Muscat Bikes LLC. The 240km long course starts and finishes at Qurum Park in Muscat, travels through the eastern Hajar foothills/Quriyat area to Wadi Dayqah Dam — the turnaround point, at a modest ~400m high point — and returns to Muscat; the 140km short course starts near Al Massara Hospital/Arqi Loop, roughly 50km into the long route, and merges with the corresponding 240km groups. It's a pre-dawn ride (5:45 AM start): the organizer publishes support cars, an ambulance, and group mechanical support along the route, plus police assistance at the start/finish area and select road crossings (not a full route-long closure). Riders receive finisher medals rather than a ranked overall classification, though the organizer has run at least one Strava-based 'Fastest Climber' segment challenge alongside the main ride. Signature challenge: Nearly 2,140m of accumulated rolling climbing over 240km in the eastern Hajar foothills despite a modest ~400m high point — sustained terrain rather than a single defining climb, ridden from a 5:45 AM pre-dawn start. Wadi Dayqah Challenge is an annually-run road cycling endurance event organized by Muscat Bikes LLC, a Muscat-based cycling retailer rather than a national federation. It uses Wadi Dayqah Dam as its turnaround point on the 240km long course, though the ride starts and finishes in Muscat (Qurum Park), not at the dam itself — so 'Wadi Dayqah' names the destination, not the whole location. It's a supported but largely non-competitive ride: the organizer publishes support cars, an ambulance, and mechanical support, plus police assistance at the start/finish and select crossings — but riders receive finisher medals rather than an overall ranked classification (the organizer has separately run a Strava-based 'Fastest Climber' segment challenge). The prior profile's elevation was blank; the organizer's own route page states roughly 2,138m of climbing on the long course against a modest ~400m high point — real rolling terrain in the Hajar foothills, not altitude, and prior promotional material rounds this figure up to about 2,300m. Consider it if you're based in or traveling to Muscat and want a genuine, organized long ride through Omani terrain with real logistical support. It is not a scored race — go in expecting a supported endurance ride, not competitive classification.

### Superior Morgul Road Race
Tier 2 | Score: 57/100 | 56 mi | 6,000 ft | Superior, Boulder County, Colorado, USA | May | gran_fondo
Profile: https://roadielabs.com/race/superior-morgul-road-race/
Markdown: https://roadielabs.com/race/superior-morgul-road-race.md

Colorado's most storied road racing circuit — The Wall, the Coors Classic, LeMond, and American Flyers. History on two wheels. A 7-mile paved circuit on Highway 128, fully closed to traffic. Wide, smooth asphalt through rolling Colorado Front Range terrain. The course is dominated by one feature: The Wall (Super Flag Hill), a steep climb of approximately 750 vertical feet that riders face on every lap. The Wall is the selection point — it is where the race is won and lost on every lap. Between climbs, the course rolls through open grassland with views of the Flatirons. Wind on the exposed loop can fracture a field. The corner at McCaslin Boulevard is the tactical setup point — positioning into The Wall determines who attacks and who suffers. For the Pro/1/2 category doing 8 laps, the cumulative fatigue of repeated Wall efforts is the race's defining challenge. Signature challenge: The Wall (Super Flag Hill) — repeated every lap. For Pro/1/2 riders doing 8 laps, that is 8 times up the most historically significant climb in American road racing. The cumulative fatigue of repeated Wall efforts, combined with wind on the exposed loop and tactical positioning at McCaslin Boulevard, makes this a race that rewards power, repeatability, and racing intelligence. The Superior Morgul Road Race is not the biggest race on the calendar. It is not the hardest. It is not the most prestigious event in its current form. But the ground you race on carries more American cycling history per square meter than almost anywhere else in the country. The Morgul-Bismarck circuit hosted the Red Zinger and Coors Classic — the races that introduced America to professional road cycling. LeMond, Hinault, Phinney, Carpenter, and Kiefel attacked The Wall here. Kevin Costner charged up it in American Flyers. The 1987 National Championships were decided on this loop. Today it is a regional circuit race organized by passionate locals. The field is Colorado-strong, not nationally deep. The course is a modified 7-mile version of the original 13-mile Morgul-Bismarck, compressed by suburban development. But when you crest The Wall and see the crowd lining the road, you are standing where American cycling stood up. Yes if American cycling history moves you and you want to race the same circuit as LeMond and Hinault. Yes if you are a Colorado road racer looking for a well-organized circuit race on closed roads as the finale of a big Superville Stage Race weekend. Skip if you're chasing state championship stakes — that's the Time Trial the day before, not this race — or if you want a long-distance endurance event with a nationally competitive field.

### GFNY NYC
Tier 2 | Score: 54/100 | 85 mi | 6,371 ft | George Washington Bridge (NJ side) / Fort Lee, NJ | May | gran_fondo
Profile: https://roadielabs.com/race/gfny-nyc/
Markdown: https://roadielabs.com/race/gfny-nyc.md

The most international peloton in the world, starting on the George Washington Bridge — GFNY NYC is a brand that outgrew its course. A grand departure from the George Washington Bridge into the leafy hills of NJ and NY, with modest climbing that doesn't match the event's outsized reputation. Since Bear Mountain was removed in 2023, the course lost its crown jewel — a 7.4km Cat 2 that gave the route genuine mountain character. What remains is a pleasant rolling ride through the Palisades with a few punchy climbs and an 18% wall on Cheesecote. Signature challenge: Cheesecote Mountain — the 18% initial ramp is a rude wake-up call after 60km. Short but it breaks rhythm badly. GFNY NYC is a strange contradiction. The brand is genuinely impressive — 30+ events worldwide, 90+ nationalities in the field, legitimate anti-doping program, and now a UCI pro race. But the course itself, especially after Bear Mountain's removal in 2023, is rolling suburban New Jersey that wouldn't merit a second look without the GFNY name. You're paying $350+ for the jersey, the atmosphere, and the right to race on the GWB — not for the route. Yes, if you value the competitive atmosphere, international field, and NYC setting over course quality. The GFNY brand is real — results count globally, doping tests are real, and the UCI pro race adds legitimate elite racing. Just don't expect the route to match the marketing since Bear Mountain was removed.

## Data Schema

Each race profile (JSON) contains:
- `race.name`, `race.slug`, `race.tagline`
- `race.vitals`: distance_mi, elevation_ft, location, date, terrain_types, field_size
- `race.fondo_rating`: overall_score, tier, 14 dimension scores + cultural_impact, discipline
- `race.course_description`: character, suffering_zones, signature_challenge
- `race.terrain`: primary, surface, technical_rating, features
- `race.climate`: primary, description, challenges
- `race.logistics`: airport, lodging_strategy, official_site
- `race.history`: founded, origin_story, notable_moments
- `race.final_verdict`: one_liner, should_you_race, alternatives
- `race.non_negotiables`: training requirements with deadlines
- `race.citations`: source URLs
- `race.tire_recommendations`: primary tires, pressure tables

Access individual profiles at: https://roadielabs.com/race/{slug}/
Machine-readable JSON index: https://roadielabs.com/search/race-index.json
